speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the ulcer, such as the shape of the base and whether there are raised or rolled edges? When did the lesion first appear, and have there been any changes in its size or pain level since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR). REQUEST TEST: Tissue biopsy of the ulcer edge for histopathology and acid-fast bacilli stain. Are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications for your Crohn's disease or uveitis?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Sarcoidosis (Majocchi's granuloma variant) secondary to immunosuppression, though Leprosy (Hansen's disease) must be ruled out given the diabetic history and rolled edges.
